native_mechanisms: Hang the two symbol strings on crossed rows of posts so their crossings form a lattice of cells, each cell's value chosen by the two symbols meeting there (match / slip-out / slip-in).
Fold the lattice along its slanting diagonal so all cells whose row+column sum is equal press into a single crease, processed crease by crease instead of row by row.
Read three stacked crease-layers at once (diagonal, up, left) and release the spent bottom layer, keeping only the two most recent creases as the fold advances.
core_technique: Anti-diagonal (wavefront) Needleman-Wunsch: each k = i+j anti-diagonal computed from the two previous ones in three rotating buffers, vectorized with AVX2 (int16 with a 32-bit fallback above the range guard) using a reversed copy of b so the diagonal's symbol pairs are contiguous, plus a scalar small-n path.
